group: q|what is a top 1% elo rating on lichess blitz

result.why: The only primary source for this is Lichess's own weekly blitz rating distribution page (https://lichess.org/stat/rating/distribution/blitz). The page currently reports 712,517 blitz players this week, but its per-rating frequency data loads through a script, and none of the fetch methods tried could read it (WebFetch directly, WebFetch through r.jina.ai). Downloading the raw HTML with curl was blocked pending approval. The only published percentile thresholds found are a user-compiled table in a Lichess forum thread ('lichess ratings and stats 2025', https://lichess.org/forum/general-chess-discussion/lichess-ratings-and-stats-2025). It gives no date and does not name its source. It lists blitz 2300 = better than 98.2% (rank ~13,000), 2400 = better than 99.1% (rank ~5,800) and 2500 = better than 99.6% (rank ~2,500), which would put the top 1% at about 2400 Lichess blitz (Glicko-2). Forum posts are excluded as sources, and that table could not be checked against the Lichess page, so the 2400 figure is unverified and is not reported as a finding. Other comparison figures, kept out for the same reasons: a GitHub analysis of the Lichess game database (jcw024/lichess_database_ETL) cites a blitz p90 of 2075 from the live Lichess page and 1927 from its own data, with no p99. Older forum posts put ~2362–2365 at the 98.8th–99.1st percentile. To resolve this, approve one curl download of the distribution page (its embedded frequency array gives exact cumulative percentiles for active players this week). Or query the Lichess API (/api/user/{name}/perf/blitz, which returns a 'percentile' field) for a few players rated 2350–2450. Possible new_metric if it ships: id chess_rating_lichess_blitz, unit points, direction high, format number, base noun 'Lichess blitz players active this week'. It is a different scale from the catalogue's chess_rating_fide.
